sentences.text: Lycorhinus was a small herbivorous dinosaur measuring about 1.2 meters in length.
This animal possessed long canines in its jaws, specifically two long, narrow canine-like teeth that projected downward from the front of its jaw.
It used its beak to pull off shoots and chewed them using its wide, flat cheek teeth.
Two long, narrow canine-like teeth projected downward from the front of Lycorhinus's jaw.
Extensive tooth-to-tooth wear facets support the hypothesis that Lycorhinus was predominantly or exclusively herbivorous.
The genus Lycorhinus was described by Sidney H. Haughton in 1924.
Lycorhinus is known from the single species L. angustidens, originally described as a cynodont from a partial jaw found in the Upper Elliot Formation of South Africa.
Specimens of Lycorhinus were collected prior to 1914 by Dr. Martin Ricono from the Red Beds of Paballong in South Africa.
Fossils of Lycorhinus, consisting of loose teeth and a maxilla, were discovered in the Cape Province of the Upper Elliot Formation in South Africa.
Christopher Gow described a nearly complete maxilla found in the Red Beds at the "buck camp" of Golden Gate Highlands National Park.
Robert Broom incorrectly identified the type locality of Lycorhinus as Witkop near Burgersdorp in a 1932 review.
Lycorhinus usually walked on four legs but could run on its hind legs with its tail held upright when it perceived danger.
Lycorhinus lived in semi-desert environments and fed on vegetation.
Barrett suggested in 2000 that Lycorhinus was likely omnivorous based on its teeth and canine.
Butler and colleagues suggested in 2008 that Lycorhinus used its canines for defense and occasional omnivory.
Porro and colleagues suggested in 2010 that Lycorhinus ate tough, fibrous vegetation.
Norman et al. suggested in 2011 that Lycorhinus did not use its canines for display or cropping vegetation.
Lycorhinus is classified as a heterodontosaurid ornithischian dinosaur.
Lycorhinus is classified in the family Heterodontosauridae.
Lycorhinus and Heterodontosaurus form the base of the family Heterodontosauridae.
Crompton and Charig identified Lycorhinus as an ornithischian in 1962.
Romer classified Lycorhinus as a member of the ornithopod family Hypsilophodontidae.
The Paleobiology Database lists Abrictosaurus consors as the type species for the genus Lycorhinus.
Specimens from the Clarens Formation have been tentatively allied with Lycorhinus but may belong to indeterminate heterodontosaurids.
Lycorhinus lived during the Early Jurassic, specifically the Sinemurian stage.
Uranium-lead dating in 2020 confirmed the Upper Elliot Formation spans from approximately 201.3 mya to at least 191.9 mya.
The Upper Elliot Formation, where Lycorhinus was found, spans from the Hettangian to the Sinemurian stages, approximately 201.3 to 190.8 million years ago.
Lycorhinus lived during the early Jurassic, approximately 203 to 197 million years ago, in what is now Africa.
The genus Lycorhinus is recorded from the Hettangian to Pliensbachian stages, between 201.4 and 184.2 million years ago.
Charig and Crompton considered Lycorhinus a nomen dubium (dubious name) due to insufficient material to determine if it was the same genus as Heterodontosaurus.
Hopson argued that Lycorhinus is a valid diagnostic genus distinct from Heterodontosaurus and Abrictosaurus.
Lycorhinus consors was considered a nomen dubium because its description was inadequate.
In 1978, Thulborn maintained that Heterodontosaurus tucki and Abrictosaurus consors were species of Lycorhinus but proposed that Lanasaurus might not be a heterodontosaurid.
Thulborn proposed in 1970 that Lycorhinus and Heterodontosaurus were synonyms.
Christopher Gow concluded in 1990 that the holotype of Lanasaurus scalpridens was actually a specimen of Lycorhinus angustidens, a view commonly accepted since then.
